must_fix: Requirement 1 ('the system shall respond'): no stimulus, no definition of 'respond', no time bound. Name the trigger, expected response content and a deadline, e.g. valid GET /items/{id} returns HTTP 200 with JSON within 500 ms at p95 under 100 concurrent users.

Requirement 2 ('users can do things quickly'): 'things', 'quickly' and 'users' are all undefined. Pick the task, user class, measurable limit and conditions, e.g. first-time user completes checkout in 3 minutes or less in 90% of moderated sessions (n >= 10).

Requirement 3 ('data is stored'): no data scope, trigger, location, retention or verification, and no 'shall' or actor. State what is persisted, when, how it is retrieved, and retention, e.g. order record persisted before confirmation, retrievable unchanged after restart, retained 7 years.
should_fix: For each rewritten requirement, confirm you can state one test with a pass/fail threshold. If you can't, it is still not ready.
structured_output.summary: All three requirements are untestable as written: they lack triggers, measurable thresholds and scope. Send all three back for rewrite using the suggested measurable forms.
